title: Didn't My Lord Deliver Daniel
description: The spiritual as the Fisk Jubilee Singers first printed it, in unison, here set for 2 to 4 singers: everyone sings the refrain in harmony, the soprano sings each verse alone, and everyone joins its last line. Three verses, each into the refrain. Steady and rhythmic, in a minor key.

credits.words: traditional spiritual, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers (published 1872)
credits.tune: traditional spiritual, as sung by the Fisk Jubilee Singers (published 1872)

licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella (the source prints the tune alone, "Sung in Unison")
licence.source: tune and words from Theodore F. Seward, ed., Jubilee Songs: Complete. As Sung by the Jubilee Singers of Fisk University (Biglow & Main, New York, 1872), pp. 16 to 17, "Didn't my Lord deliver Daniel", "Sung in Unison" (Seward died 1902; the words taken down by George L. White, who died 1895), checked note for note against J. B. T. Marsh, The Story of the Jubilee Singers; With Their Songs (1881), No. 10, pp. 134 to 135; in G minor, 4/8, as printed, written here a tone up in A minor, in 2/4 with the printed values doubled (a printed eighth is a beat); the refrain, then verses 1, 2 and 4 of the 4, each into the refrain; Seward's footnote, "Go on without pause, leaving out two beats of the measure", is not followed: each verse's last word is held one beat and a beat's rest restored, for a breath; the third "Dan-iel," of each refrain is sung an eighth shorter, its "iel" an eighth earlier, for a breath; read from the scan at archive.org/details/jubileesongscomp00sewa
